clue.text: Dress Oscar in the woman's footwear

indicators.note: one item sitting in another means it is placed inside that word

blocks.note: to deck is to dress or adorn
the pronoun for a woman
Oscar is O in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A woman's shoes are dressed up with an Oscar, as if for an awards night.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'is', linking wordplay to definition; 'Dress' looks like a garment but is a verb meaning adorn.
explanation.definitionFit: A deck shoe is a casual canvas or leather shoe with a grippy sole, originally worn on boats.

clue.text: Quack from teal on river, initially, after fish turned up

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning a word up makes it read from bottom to top
initially points at the opening letter of each of the words before it

blocks.note: the cod is a common fish
the first letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A sham remedy made from a duck on a river, following some fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quack' and 'teal' set up a duck scene; the quack is in fact the slang word for a medic.
explanation.definitionFit: Quack is informal, usually jokey slang for a medical practitioner, not only a fraudulent one.

clue.text: Comfortable houses in Europe?

indicators.note: a word that houses another holds it within its walls

blocks.note: content means comfortable and satisfied
taken as written

explanation.surface: A question about whether European homes are comfortable.
explanation.walkthrough: CONT(IN)ENT. Britons call mainland Europe 'the Continent'; the question mark flags that Europe is an example of a continent.
explanation.definitionFit: Europe is one of the world's continents, and Britons speak of mainland Europe simply as the Continent.

clue.text: Sermon only half wrong? You might experience this in church

definitions.text: You might experience this in church

indicators.note: keeping only half of a word means dropping its back three letters

blocks.note: a preacher's address, of which the first half is kept
a vice is a wrong or sin

explanation.surface: A grumble that the sermon was only partly wrong, set in a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A service is the act of worship held in a church, which a congregation attends.

clue.text: Nothing fine on X on a regular basis

blocks.note: the letter O looks like zero
F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine
here only a positional link: what follows comes next
X is ten in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Something about a fine imposed for nothing, on someone called X, happening routinely.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done often happens frequently, that is, regularly and repeatedly.

clue.text: Seasoned Conservative glimpsed on the periphery

indicators.note: one word sitting on the periphery of another surrounds it

blocks.note: to spy something is to glimpse it
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: An experienced Tory politician spotted at the edge of the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seasoned' looks like it means experienced, describing the Conservative; it is the culinary definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that is spiced has been flavoured with spices, which is one way of seasoning it.

clue.text: What one's doing at golf club? Parking

definitions.text: What one's doing at golf club?

blocks.clueFragment: What one's doing at golf club?
blocks.note: first meaning: tapping the ball towards the hole with a putter
second meaning: placing or setting something down

explanation.walkthrough: The golf-club reading suggests a clubhouse visit, then 'Parking' seems to answer it; really one is using a club on the green, and the other sense is placing something.
explanation.definitionFit: On the green a golfer is putting with a club, and to park something is to put it somewhere.

clue.text: Fool around with blue note

blocks.note: C stands for circa, Latin for around
feeling blue is feeling low
N is the abbreviation for note

explanation.surface: An instruction to mess about with a sad note in a piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fool around' looks like a single phrasal verb; split it, and 'around' is the abbreviation c.
explanation.definitionFit: A clown is a fool, someone who plays the joker for laughs.

clue.text: Penny is sitting on plant — catastrophe!

blocks.note: D was the abbreviation for the old British penny
taken as written
in a down entry, sitting on means placed above what follows
the aster is a daisy-like garden flower

explanation.surface: Someone called Penny has sat on a plant, ruining it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penny' reads as a woman's name; it is the old penny, abbreviated d.
explanation.definitionFit: A disaster is a sudden calamity, the same as a catastrophe.

clue.text: Former lover getting on with female? Hard to believe

blocks.note: someone getting on is ageing
joins the next part on
F is the abbreviation for female
a lame excuse is weak and hard to believe

explanation.surface: An ex said to be getting on well with another woman — unlikely!
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting on with' looks like a phrase about friendship; here it splits into 'getting on', meaning ageing, and the link 'with'.
explanation.definitionFit: An old flame is an idiom for a past romantic partner.

clue.text: Cream can tour a lot and sing 1968 hit

indicators.note: to cream ingredients is to beat them together until they blend into a new mixture

blocks.note: taken as written for the mix
taken as written for the mix

explanation.surface: The rock band Cream can go on tour a lot and perform a hit from 1968.
explanation.walkthrough: Cream reads as the 1960s band, a fine piece of misdirection; it is the cookery verb. Congratulations was Cliff Richard's 1968 Eurovision song.
explanation.definitionFit: Congratulations was a 1968 number-one single for Cliff Richard, the UK's Eurovision entry that year.

clue.text: Feeling old, one breaks two legs

indicators.note: something that breaks into a word forces its way into the middle of it

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
pins is slang for legs, and on is the leg side in cricket
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An elderly person feels that one fall has broken both legs.
explanation.walkthrough: Pins is informal for legs; in cricket the on side is also called the leg side, so ON is a second leg.
explanation.definitionFit: An opinion is a view or belief, as in 'my feeling is that...'.

clue.text: Devotees hugging queen's companions

indicators.note: a word hugging another wraps its arms around it

blocks.note: a fiend is an enthusiast, as in a fitness fiend
R is for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: Royal fans embracing the Queen's companions.
explanation.walkthrough: R (Regina) goes inside FIENDS; the 's is read as 'is', linking to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Friends are companions, people whose company you keep.

clue.text: Made with rare, refined sugar

indicators.note: refining something reprocesses it into a new form

blocks.note: taken as written for the mix
taken as written for the mix

explanation.surface: Something cooked rare with refined sugar.
explanation.walkthrough: Refined sits naturally with sugar, which is the answer's own world; here it acts on the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Demerara is a light brown, coarse cane sugar named after a region of Guyana.

clue.text: Presumed father's upset with mother?

indicators.note: in a down entry, upset means turned upside down, so the word reads upwards

blocks.note: pa is an informal word for father
joins the next part on
a mother is an example of a parent

explanation.surface: Suggests that Dad is assumed to be annoyed with Mum.
explanation.walkthrough: PA reversed gives AP, followed by PARENT; the 's is read as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparent means seeming or presumed, as an heir apparent is presumed to inherit.

clue.text: Elegance from good people

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
a race is a people or nation

explanation.surface: Fine manners displayed by decent folk.
explanation.definitionFit: Grace is poise and elegance of movement or manner.

clue.text: Excitement from organising nude rave — about time!

indicators.note: organising things arranges them into a new order
about means going around something else and enclosing it

blocks.note: taken as written for the mix
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled to be finally putting on a naked dance party.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters go around T; 'about time' reads as 'at last!', but here 'about' acts on time.
explanation.definitionFit: An adventure is an exciting, risky experience, so the word stands for excitement.

clue.text: People who check crowns — different kinds — test if king's scratched

indicators.note: different signals that the letters must be made into something other than they are
a scratched runner is withdrawn from a race, so this letter is removed

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
K is the chess abbreviation for king; this is the letter dropped

explanation.surface: Royal inspectors who examine crowns, testing whether the king has been scratched.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove K from KINDS TEST and rearrange the rest. 'Crowns' suggests royalty, but these are crowns on teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Dentists examine and fit crowns, the caps placed over damaged teeth.

clue.text: T-Rex traditionally eats more than necessary

indicators.note: what the phrase eats is swallowed whole inside its run of letters

blocks.note: found spanning the end of the dinosaur's name and the start of the next word

explanation.surface: A tyrannosaurus has always eaten too much.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen and the word break hide the join: t-r(EX TRA)ditionally.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra means surplus, more than is needed or usual.

clue.text: Article not genuine? Editor's embarrassed

blocks.note: a is the indefinite article
a sham is a fake
ed. is the standard abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: An editor is mortified that a newspaper article turned out to be fake.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'is', linking the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashamed means feeling guilt or embarrassment over something done.

clue.text: Keep quiet, respecting tennis player's first shot

blocks.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
re means regarding or respecting
every tennis point begins with a serve

explanation.surface: Advice to stay silent about a tennis player's opening stroke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep quiet' reads as one phrase; split it, and Keep is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To preserve is to keep something safe or maintain it in its present state.

clue.text: Forgives previous girlfriend, say, then swears Romeo's vanished

indicators.note: something that has vanished is no longer present, so this letter goes

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner; say marks the girlfriend as one example
to curse is to swear
Romeo is R in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone pardons a former partner, then curses because Romeo has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: R is taken from CURSES; the 's is read as 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: To excuse someone is to pardon or forgive them for a fault.

clue.text: Divulges missing end of tea parties

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter
missing means lacking something, so that letter is taken away

blocks.note: to divulge a secret is to reveal it
the last letter of tea

explanation.surface: Someone gives away secrets about tea parties but leaves out how they ended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tea parties' reads as one phrase; parties stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Revels are lively celebrations, festivities or parties.

clue.text: Term almost enthrals every schoolmaster?

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is cut
to enthral once meant to hold captive, so one word holds the other

blocks.note: taken as written, minus its last letter
each and every are synonyms

explanation.surface: A school term nearly captivates every master.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark shows that a schoolmaster is one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A schoolmaster is a male teacher at a school, so it is an example of the general word.

clue.text: Tolerate a US president? Not quite

indicators.note: not quite means falling just short, so the final letter is cut

blocks.note: taken as written
Joe Biden was the 46th US president

explanation.surface: A question about whether a certain American president can be put up with.
explanation.definitionFit: To abide something is to bear or endure it, as in 'I can't abide noise'.

clue.text: I regularly clean church after Cardinal finally gives permission

indicators.note: finally points at the closing letter of the word before it
regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: the last letter of Cardinal
taken as written
the first, third and fifth letters
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A cardinal finally authorises someone to clean the church regularly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gives permission' looks like the definition but the noun is wanted; gives is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A licence is formal permission to do something, or the document granting it.

clue.text: Some alcohol a colleague picked up for boozer

indicators.note: some means a part of the phrase, so the answer lies within it
in a down entry, picking something up lifts it so it reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of the first word into the last

explanation.surface: Drinks fetched for a colleague who likes a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boozer' looks like a drinker; in British slang it is a pub, and the local is your nearest pub.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain 'the local' is the pub nearest your home, and boozer is slang for a pub.

clue.text: Bikini? Mum's is wet and coming off

indicators.note: off means gone bad or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written for the mix, including the s
taken as written for the mix

explanation.surface: A mother's bikini is soaked and falling off: a beach mishap.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a bikini as one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bikini is a two-piece example of the clothing worn for swimming.

clue.text: Zooms around sea in ship

indicators.note: turning around makes the word face the other way
one item placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship
the deep is a poetic word for the sea

explanation.surface: A vessel racing about on the open water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around sea' looks like going round the ocean; here around turns the deep backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To speed is to go very fast, as to zoom is.

clue.text: Keep on cutting short person? These could protect wounds

indicators.note: something short is lacking its end, so the word is cut down
a word cutting another slices into it and sits in the middle

blocks.note: to last is to keep on going
taken as written, then shortened

explanation.surface: Someone keeps nicking a short man, so dressings are needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims the word to its first four letters. In Britain plasters are sticking plasters, adhesive bandages.
explanation.definitionFit: Plasters are the British name for adhesive dressings put over cuts, so they protect wounds.
